questions.question: First-pass yield, scrap and rework by product line, hw rev, station and site — where is yield eroding, and since when?
questions.verdict_headline: Trailing 3-month window 2026-06..2026-08: portfolio first-pass yield 96.6% on 10970 units started (down 0.1 pts vs the prior 3 months); 0 of 5 lines below the 95% floor; 2 of 20 line×station cells below the floor: PP3500 · test 93.5% since 2026-04, IP5000 · test 94.9% since 2026-04; erosion is rev-specific — PP3500 rev C at test 92.5% vs other revs 96.1%, below the floor since 2026-04; scrap 1.0%, rework 2.4% of units started

question.what: The plant's yield review: what share of units pass each step the first time, cut by product line, hardware revision, station, and site — and, for any cell below the floor, the month the erosion started.
question.why: Yield erosion is the earliest, cheapest place to catch a process or design problem. The cuts tell the plant manager whether the fix belongs to one revision, one station, or one site — and how long it has been going on.

fpy-stat.label: First-pass yield
fpy-stat.what: Units passed first time divided by units started over the trailing window, with the scrap and rework rates that make up the failures.
fpy-stat.why: The headline health check for the plant; read against the yield floor.
fpy-stat.how_to_read: Higher is better; scrap plus rework equals the first-pass failure rate.

fpy-by-line.what: First-pass yield per product line over the trailing window.
fpy-by-line.why: Names which product's process is eroding; one line can breach while the portfolio stays inside the floor.

fpy-by-station.what: First-pass yield per line station (SMT, final assembly, test, pack).
fpy-by-station.why: Locates the step where units fail — a test-station dip and an assembly dip need different owners.

fpy-by-site.why: Separates a product problem from a plant problem.

scrap-rework-by-line.what: Scrap rate and rework rate per product line.
scrap-rework-by-line.why: Rework hides problems (the unit still ships); scrap destroys value. The split says which cost the yield loss is taking.

erosion-cells.what: Every product-line × station cell below the yield floor in the window, with the first month of its current run below the floor.
erosion-cells.why: Answers 'since when' with a computed date instead of a recollection — the onset month is where the investigation starts.
erosion-cells.how_to_read: A cell that dipped and recovered is not listed; only cells still below the floor at the as-of date appear.

pp3500-rev-by-station.what: PP3500 first-pass yield by hardware revision and station.
pp3500-rev-by-station.why: Tells a revision-specific defect apart from a station-wide drift — the difference between a design-transfer problem and a process problem.

fpy-trend.what: Monthly first-pass yield for the portfolio and for the revision/station cell with the widest yield gap.
fpy-trend.why: Shows whether the erosion is a step change, a slide, or a recovery in progress.

verdict.what: The verdict names the portfolio yield, how many lines and cells sit below the floor, the revision-specific gap, and the onset month.
verdict.why: It keeps a healthy portfolio average from hiding one eroding revision at one station.

terms.definition: The share of units that pass a production step the first time, without rework or scrap. It is the cleanest single measure of whether a process is under control: yield that erodes means defects are being made faster than the process catches them.
The two exits from a first-pass failure — a unit is either scrapped (discarded) or reworked (repaired and re-tested). Both cost money; rework also hides process problems because the unit still ships.

questions.question: Capacity vs the demand plan — can each line and site build the planned units, and where is the constraint?
NCR rate and aging, CAPA open count, past-due share and effectiveness-verification backlog — by source and severity.
questions.verdict_headline: At 2026-08-31: 32 open CAPAs, 21 past due (66%), 5 critical past due; past-due count rising (6 six months earlier → 21); effectiveness verified on 28 of 47 closed CAPAs (60% vs 90% floor, backlog 19); 19 open NCRs (9 past due, mean age 129 d), NCR intake 11.7/month vs 10.7 prior; supplier NCRs concentrate on SUP-003 (21 of 45, 47%)

question.what: The quality-system backlog review: how many nonconformances and CAPAs are open, how many are past due, how old they are, where they come from, and whether closed CAPAs were verified effective.
question.why: Past-due CAPAs and unverified closures are what an auditor finds first. The cuts by source and severity say whether the load is a supplier problem, a production problem, or a capacity problem in the quality team.

capa-stat.label: CAPA posture
capa-stat.what: Open CAPAs, past-due open CAPAs, the effectiveness-verified share of closed CAPAs, and open NCRs — all at the data's as-of date.
capa-stat.why: The four numbers a quality VP is asked for in a management review.

capa-pastdue-trend.what: Open and past-due open CAPAs at each month-end, rebuilt from each record's opened, due, and closed dates.
capa-pastdue-trend.why: Says whether the backlog is growing or being worked down — a rising past-due line is the aging signal.

ncr-trend.what: Nonconformance reports opened per month, all sources and supplier-sourced.
ncr-trend.why: The intake rate; a rising supplier line points at purchased parts rather than the plant's own process.

capa-open-by-source.what: Open and past-due CAPAs by where the problem was found (production, supplier, complaint, audit, field).
capa-open-by-source.why: Field- and complaint-sourced CAPAs past due carry patient-safety and regulatory weight the others do not.

capa-open-by-severity.what: Open and past-due CAPAs by severity.
capa-open-by-severity.why: A critical CAPA past due is the finding that should never appear.

ncr-open-by-severity.what: Open NCRs by severity, with the mean days since each was opened.
ncr-open-by-severity.why: Aging NCRs are undispositioned material and unresolved process questions.

ncr-by-source.what: Nonconformance reports opened in the trailing three months, by source.
ncr-by-source.why: Where the recent nonconformance load is coming from.

effectiveness-by-quarter.what: Closed CAPAs per closure quarter, split into effectiveness-verified and not.
effectiveness-by-quarter.why: Shows whether verification is keeping pace with closure or falling behind as a backlog.

supplier-ncr-concentration.why: One supplier driving most of the supplier NCRs is a sourcing decision, not a plant decision.

verdict.what: The verdict carries the open and past-due CAPA counts, the critical past-due count, the verified share against its floor, the open-NCR count and age, and the top supplier's share.
verdict.why: Each count survives a one-line rollup so the badge never hides a critical item behind a healthy total.

terms.definition: The formal record raised when a product, material, or process does not meet its specification. Every NCR has to be investigated and dispositioned (use as is, rework, scrap, return to supplier). The rate and age of open NCRs show how much unresolved quality work the plant is carrying.

Corrective And Preventive Action — the quality-system process for formally investigating a problem, fixing its root cause, and preventing recurrence. A CAPA past its due date is an acknowledged problem the company has not yet fixed on the schedule it set itself.

The final step of a CAPA: checking, after the fix has been in place, that the problem actually stopped recurring. A CAPA closed without effectiveness verification is a fix that has been asserted, not demonstrated.

questions.question: Lot release lead time and DHR completeness — where are lots queuing before release, and is it getting worse?
Supplier quality — incoming reject rate and on-time by supplier and component family, scorecard distribution, single-source exposure, audit currency.
questions.verdict_headline: Incoming reject rate 2.3% across 12 suppliers in 2026-06..2026-08 (2639 lots received), on-time 93.4%; 3 supplier(s) above the 3% ceiling: SUP-003 7.9% single-source, SUP-006 6.5% probation, SUP-011 4.3% conditional; 1 audit(s) overdue (SUP-003 by 289 d); 2 single-source supplier(s) (pump-motor, display); scorecards A 4 / B 5 / C 1 / D 2

question.what: The supplier-quality review: which suppliers are rejecting parts at incoming inspection or delivering late, how the scorecards are distributed, which components depend on a single supplier, and whose audits are overdue.
question.why: A failing single-source supplier stops the line; an overdue audit means the company is buying from controls it has not verified. Both are sourcing decisions the plant cannot make alone.

supplier-stat.label: Incoming quality
supplier-stat.what: Reject rate and on-time delivery across all suppliers in the trailing window, plus how many suppliers breach the ceiling and how many audits are overdue.
supplier-stat.why: The headline for the supplier-quality review.

reject-by-supplier.what: Share of incoming lots rejected per supplier over the trailing window.
reject-by-supplier.why: Names the suppliers whose parts are failing on arrival.
reject-by-supplier.how_to_read: Lower is better; compare against the reject ceiling.

ontime-by-supplier.what: On-time delivery per supplier over the trailing window.
ontime-by-supplier.why: Late parts starve the line even when they are good parts.

reject-by-family.what: Incoming reject rate per component family.
reject-by-family.why: A family-level problem (all battery suppliers rejecting) points at the specification; a supplier-level one points at the supplier.

scorecard-distribution.what: How many suppliers hold each scorecard grade in the latest period.
scorecard-distribution.why: The shape of the supply base at a glance.

single-source-exposure.what: The suppliers that are the only approved source for their component, with their reject rate, grade, and audit status.
single-source-exposure.why: These are the suppliers whose failure has no fallback.

audit-currency.what: Days until each supplier's next audit is due; negative means overdue.
audit-currency.why: An overdue audit on a single-source supplier is the combination that should trigger action.

reject-trend.what: Monthly incoming reject rate for all suppliers and for each supplier above the ceiling.
reject-trend.why: Distinguishes a bad month from a deteriorating supplier.

verdict.what: The verdict names the overall reject rate, the suppliers above the ceiling (with single-source and status flags), overdue audits, the single-source families, and the scorecard distribution.
verdict.why: It keeps a healthy average from hiding one single-source supplier that is failing.

terms.definition: The check performed on purchased components and materials when they arrive, before they enter production. The incoming reject rate is the earliest signal that a supplier's quality is slipping.

A component with exactly one approved supplier. If that supplier fails an audit, stops shipping, or ships defective parts, production stops with it — there is no second source to switch to without a requalification effort.

A periodic grade (A to D) a company assigns each supplier from its quality and delivery performance. It turns many measurements into one signal that drives audit frequency, sampling intensity, and sourcing decisions.

Whether a supplier's most recent quality-system audit is within the interval the company's procedure requires. An overdue audit means the company is buying from a supplier whose controls it has not recently verified.

A label on every figure saying where it came from — measured (read directly from a pinned dataset), derived (computed from pinned data by a stated formula), assumed (an explicit assumption record), or unavailable (the data does not exist and the gap is stated, not filled).

questions.question: Component obsolescence risk by hardware revision — which parts on which revs are single-sourced, end-of-life, or on conditional suppliers?
Recall scoping via lot genealogy — if a component lot or process window is implicated, which finished lots and fleet devices are affected?
Process-validation and calibration posture — overdue and due items by site and product line, and the blockers for PP3500 rev C release.
questions.verdict_headline: At 2026-08-31: 10 overdue and 6 due-within-30-day items across 155 register entries; overdue calibrations Eastbrook 1, Westfield 9 — the cluster is at Westfield; PP3500 rev C release blockers: 3 validation item(s) not validated (PQ in-progress due 2026-09-30, PQ in-progress due 2026-09-30, OQ not-started due 2026-10-15) and 4 DHR-incomplete lot(s); 65 rev C lots already released since 2026-03-25 while the fixture PQ is still in-progress

question.what: The validation and metrology status review: which equipment and processes are overdue or coming due for validation, calibration, or maintenance, by site and product line — and what is still open on the PP3500 rev C production path.
question.why: Producing on unvalidated processes or measuring with out-of-calibration instruments puts every affected lot in question. The rev C view says what must close before that revision can be released cleanly.

posture-stat.label: Validation & calibration posture
posture-stat.what: Overdue items, items due within the window, overdue calibrations by site, and the count of open rev C blockers.
posture-stat.why: The numbers a quality VP takes to the plant review.

posture-by-site.what: Overdue and due-soon register items per plant.
posture-by-site.why: Locates the metrology or validation backlog to a site and its owner.

posture-by-type.what: Overdue and due-soon items by record type (IQ, OQ, PQ, calibration, preventive maintenance).
posture-by-type.why: A calibration backlog and a validation backlog have different owners and different lot impact.

posture-by-line.what: Overdue and due-soon items by product line (shared equipment listed separately).
posture-by-line.why: Says which product's lots are exposed.

overdue-calibrations.what: Each overdue calibration with the days past due.
overdue-calibrations.why: The longest-overdue instruments define how far back the lot-impact assessment must reach.

revc-blockers.what: PP3500 rev C validation items (fixtures, processes) not yet validated, with status, due date, and owner.
revc-blockers.why: The validation-side checklist for releasing rev C.

revc-lots.what: PP3500 rev C lots by release state: released, in process, or blocked by an incomplete device history record.
revc-lots.why: Blocked lots are finished inventory that cannot ship; released lots while validation is open are a question for the design-transfer record.

posture-history.what: How overdue and due-soon counts have moved over time — not available from a single snapshot.
posture-history.why: Stated as a gap so the reader does not mistake one snapshot for a trend; recurring snapshots build it.

verdict.what: The verdict carries the overdue and due-soon counts, the overdue calibrations by site, each open rev C validation item, the blocked-lot count, and how many rev C lots were released while validation is open.
verdict.why: Each element survives a one-line rollup; the released-while-open count is the item a reviewer must not miss.

terms.definition: Documented evidence that a piece of equipment or a production process consistently produces what it is supposed to. IQ (installation qualification) shows it is installed correctly; OQ (operational qualification) shows it works across its operating range; PQ (performance qualification) shows it performs under real production conditions. Producing on an unvalidated process is a quality-system finding.

Periodic confirmation that a measuring instrument reads correctly against a known reference. A measurement taken with an out-of-calibration instrument cannot be trusted — every lot it accepted since the due date is in question.

The per-lot production record that proves each lot was built, tested, and released according to the approved process — who did what, with which materials, and the test results. A lot cannot be released until its DHR is complete.
